_comment: skfem helmholtz#3 PML: a too-thin layer back-reflects and too-large sigma degrades absorption. Verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 on a one-element-thick MeshQuad strip (k=8, 20 elements/wavelength, 4 wavelengths of interior, 222 DOFs tuned) with s = 1 - i*sigma(x)/k assembled inside @BilinearForm(dtype=complex) as (1/s) u_x v_x + s u_y v_y - k^2 s u v and a quadratic sigma ramp. Reflection R = (SWR-1)/(SWR+1) measured on interior nodes only: no PML R = 0.97; lambda/8 layer R = 0.375; tuned 1.5 lambda with sigma_max = 2k R = 3.9e-5 (the claim's |R| < 1e-3 target); sigma_max = 2e4*k at that thickness R = 0.34. Thickness sweep is monotone and every sub-lambda/2 layer misses 1e-3 while 1-2 lambda meets it; the sigma sweep has an interior optimum. NUANCE: the claim's literal 'reflects more than it absorbs' (R > 0.5) is reached in the too-SMALL-sigma direction (sigma_max = 0.05k -> R = 0.72), not in the too-large direction, which instead degrades R by orders of magnitude. No measured floats are pinned. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 replaces both mistakes by the claim's own standard choices at their pathology sites -- THIN_THICK_LAM becomes TUNED_THICK_LAM (lambda/8 -> 1.5 lambda) and HUGE_SIGMA becomes TUNED_SIGMA (2e4*k -> 2*k) -- so both wrong variants reproduce the tuned R = 3.9e-5. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 16 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'thin_thickness_lam=0.125 thin_is_under_half_wavelength=True', 'thin_n_dofs=166', 'thin_R_gt_1e-2=True', 'thin_R_worse_than_tuned_by_gt_100x=True', 'huge_sigma_R_gt_1e-2=True', 'huge_sigma_worse_than_tuned_by_gt_1000x=True' and 'sigma_too_large_is_worse_than_optimum=True' so the fixture goes red.
